# CVReg: A Covoting Regression Model and Associated Methods

## Introduction

This package helps researchers to prepare data and estimate the covoting regression model (CVR) developed by Müller-Crepon and Bormann (APSR, forthcoming) and briefly outlined below.  
When using the method and/or package, please cite: 

Müller-Crepon, C., & Bormann, N.-C. (2025). Coethnics Covote in Africa: Studying Electoral Cleavages with a Covoting Regression Model. _American Political Science Review_, forthcoming. 

You can find the publication for all technical details [here]() and as ungated version [here](http://www.carlmueller-crepon.org/publication/ethnic_parties/).

## The method



## Installation

You can directly download and install the CVReg package from GitHub. Upon installation, the package should automatically install all necessary R dependencies. 

```{r, eval = F}
library(devtools)
# install_github(repo = "carl-mc/CVReg")
devtools::load_all(".")

```


## Preparing your data

Users of the CVR model get started by transforming their data (e.g., a survey) 
into pairwise observations. 

```{r, eval = T, warning=FALSE, message=F}
library(CVReg)
# Load some synthetic data
data("synthvote")

# Generate pairs
pair.dt <- data_to_pairs(df = synthvote, structure = "full")

# Inspect
head(pair.dt)
```

Based on the pairs of observations a and b, we can now create a series of variables 
that record similarities and shared characteristics in each pair. 
```{r, eval = T, warning=FALSE, message=F}
# Process pair level data to create pairwise similarity/difference measures
pair.dt <- process_pairs(df = pair.dt,
                         vars =  c("prtvt.eq", "group.eq", "income.sim"))

# Inspect
summary(subset(pair.dt,,c("prtvt.eq", "group.eq", "income.sim")))
```


## Fitting a CVR

Using the pair level data on covoting, shared group membership and 
income similarity, we can now run a simple linear regression model.
```{r, eval = T, warning=FALSE, message=F}
library(fixest)
lm <- feols(prtvt.eq ~ group.eq + income.sim, data = pair.dt,
            cluster = c("a.ID", "a.ID"))
summary(lm)
```

Or we can use `the estimate_cvreg()` function, which implements 
some additional methods, such as computing conditional within- and between-group
covoting probabilities, or clustered standard errors for 
dyadic data. 

```{r, eval = T, warning=FALSE, message=F}
cvr <- estimate_cvreg(prtvt.eq ~ group.eq + income.sim, data = pair.dt,
                      cvr.det.var = "group.eq", cluster = c("a.ID", "a.ID"))
all(cvr$coefficient == lm$coefficient)
summary(cvr)
unlist(cvr$sum.ls[c(1,2)])
do.call(cbind, cvr$sum.ls[-c(1,2)])
```

## Contrast with conditional covoting probabilities from multinomial model

```{r, eval = T, warning=FALSE, message=F}
est_covote_indlevel(out = "prtvt", cov = c("group", "income"), data = synthvote, method = "ols")
```


## Add cross-cleavage interaction terms for improved inference
```{r, eval = T, warning=FALSE, message=F}
m.int <- estimate_cvreg(prtvt.eq ~ group.eq + income.sim, data = pair.dt, 
                      cluster = c("a.ID", "a.ID"), main.int.var = "group.eq",
                      int.vars = c("income.sim"))
summary(m.int)
```
